---
type: wordle
title: Slope of a line from its graph
lhs: "m ="
answer: rise ÷ run
keys: rise run ÷ × + −
---

## Hint
Slope measures how **steep** a line is. In the diagram, going from $(1, 1)$ to $(4, 3)$, the line moves $3$ to the right (the run) and $2$ up (the rise).

```{.tikz}
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8]
  % grid and axes
  \draw[gray!30, very thin] (-0.5,-0.5) grid (5.5,4.5);
  \draw[-{Stealth[length=2mm]}] (-0.5,0) -- (5.7,0) node[right] {$x$};
  \draw[-{Stealth[length=2mm]}] (0,-0.5) -- (0,4.7) node[above] {$y$};
  % the line through (1,1) and (4,3)
  \draw[seg, blue!65!black] (0,0.333) -- (5,3.667);
  % run (across), then rise (up)
  \draw[seg, red!65!black, dashed] (1,1) -- node[below, font=\footnotesize] {run $= 3$} (4,1)
                                          -- node[right, font=\footnotesize] {rise $= 2$} (4,3);
  \node[center dot] at (1,1) {};
  \node[center dot] at (4,3) {};
  \node[above left, font=\footnotesize] at (1,1) {$(1, 1)$};
  \node[above left, font=\footnotesize] at (4,3) {$(4, 3)$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

## Hint
A steep line rises a lot over a short run, so its slope should be a large number. Which order of division makes that happen?

## Solution
**Answer:** $m = \frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}$

In the diagram, the rise is $2$ and the run is $3$, so $m = \frac{2}{3}$.

- **run ÷ rise**: upside down. It would give steep lines *small* slopes: here $\frac{3}{2}$ instead of $\frac{2}{3}$.
